name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines. The collection includes 11.5K multimodal questions with 30 highly heterogeneous image types such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to identify and eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format and undertaking necessary corrections. In the third stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions must contain one or more images and be written in English at college-level difficulty. Questions should not be ambiguous and can be answered with one of the given options or a short answer. Each question is categorized as either multiple-choice or open-ended. All fields are annotated, including the question, answer options for multiple-choice questions, the correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Each collected sample is stored in a separate JSON file following a standard naming rule.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects covered in the benchmark. The annotators represent diverse disciplines across Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset has undergone multiple version updates (v1 to v4 from November 2023 to June 2024), with updates including additional model results, corrections of typos, and adjustments to overall results. The live-updating leaderboard is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and will prove instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark aims to evaluate models on tasks akin to those faced by experts, potentially contributing to AI systems that could reach the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor for many industries.
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. MMMU combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, but this may not capture all aspects of expert-level reasoning. The benchmark does not provide a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the 90th percentile of skilled adults as defined in Expert AGI taxonomy.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating large multimodal models on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks. It is intended for Testing and Validation purposes. The benchmark is used to assess models' capabilities in perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse college-level subjects. It is not recommended for training purposes due to potential data contamination concerns.
